payload.chart: Rows x options (pruned cells with reasons): R1 worktree home: (a) .worktrees/ inside the repo, gitignored (discoverable from root; needs the ignore per the probe) | (b) sibling directory outside the repo (dodges git add entirely; scatters the filesystem) | (c) arbitrary user paths - PRUNED: undiscoverable, violates C4. R2 root addressing: (a) one server per worktree, session-bound root (today's shim --root, unchanged mechanics; needs one reconnect per stream for a single harness) | (b) root parameter on every tool - PRUNED: touches every schema mid-session, the exact arg-stripping trap the kickoff incident taught | (c) one server on the trunk, instance-routed (the loop discovers open instances across trunk + worktrees and serves by iteration; no schema change). R3 suspect mark: (a) frontmatter field on the node via the apply lane (Obsidian-visible, queryable, grandfather-safe) | (b) sidecar suspects file (nodes untouched but the mark hides from every reader) | (c) on-edge marks - PRUNED: the overlap is node-level by definition. R4 merge engine: (a) shell git merge + name-only fork-point analysis (probe-proven today) | (b) reimplement merge - PRUNED: violates C3/C6 for nothing | (c) rebase - PRUNED: history rewrite, SE-C-002's spirit. R5 shipped-check for depends_on: (a) instance status closed | (b) gate_release grant present in grants.jsonl (the authoritative ship record). R6 stream visibility: (a) derived at read from git worktree list + instance files (DRY law) | (b) registry file - PRUNED: a cache that WILL go stale (i16's law: derive at read).
payload.shortlist: K1 routed spine: R1a + R2c + R3a + R4a + R5b + R6a - one server, worktrees inside, instance-routed serving, frontmatter suspects. K2 server-per-tree: R1b + R2a + R3a + R4a + R5a + R6a - each stream its own shim spawn on a sibling tree; today's mechanics untouched, built for the subagent future. K3 spine-with-per-tree-option: K1's serving PLUS K2's spawn path kept legal (the shim already takes --root) - the hybrid where one agent routes centrally now and subagents bind their own trees later.
